title: Topological Superradiant Universality Classes in Cavity-Mediated Spin Chains
authors: Yunhao Liu, Sheng Yang, Mingyuan Chen, Xue-Jia Yu
abstract: Superradiant phase transitions are fundamental phenomena in light-matter coupled systems. Here, we uncover a novel class of superradiant criticality that is topologically distinct from previously known superradiant transitions. Using cavity-mediated cluster-Ising chains as an illustrative example, we numerically demonstrate that the critical line separating the superradiant phase from the cavity topological phase hosts robust symmetry-protected edge degeneracies, a feature absent in conventional superradiant transitions. Remarkably, although its local bulk critical properties are indistinguishable from those of the previously identified topologically trivial superradiant transition, the two criticalities cannot be smoothly connected without breaking the protecting symmetries or passing through a multicritical point. We further show that such topological superradiant criticality is generic, also occurring in cavity-mediated $\mathbb{Z}_{n}^{}$ cluster-qudit chains, as supported by complementary lattice simulations.
summary: This work characterizes a novel class of topologically distinct superradiant quantum critical points in cavity-mediated spin chains. By analyzing edge degeneracies and comparing bulk versus boundary critical behavior, the authors prove that this criticality is fundamentally different from conventional transitions. This has implications for understanding topological order in open quantum systems.
main_problem: To investigate if superradiant phase transitions can exhibit topological universality classes distinct from conventional light-matter coupled systems.
main_result: The critical line separating the superradiant phase from the cavity topological phase is topologically nontrivial, evidenced by robust symmetry-protected edge degeneracies, and this criticality is generic for cluster-qudit chains.
method: Numerical simulations, including Finite-size Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) and analysis of entanglement entropies and energy spectra.
model_or_system: The study uses cavity-mediated cluster-Ising chains (and generalizes to cluster-qudit chains) coupled to a single photon mode, described by a specific Hamiltonian involving cavity and spin interactions.
key_observables: Photon occupation number, entanglement entropies ($S_{	ext{spin}}$, $S_{	ext{photon-spin}}$), Binder cumulant, and boundary/bulk spin correlations.
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ($g, J, f$), photon frequency ($\omega_0$), and system size ($L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing bulk critical properties with boundary/edge properties to diagnose topological differences.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing three distinct phases (FM, Superradiant, SPT), and show finite-size scaling of entanglement entropies and correlation functions confirming topological differences between models.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the phase diagram, using DMRG and finite-size scaling to distinguish between topologically trivial and non-trivial critical points in the superradiant transition.
why_interesting: It bridges concepts from quantum optics (superradiance) with topological quantum matter, showing how topological invariants can characterize critical points in open quantum systems.

Spintronics.note: The study directly investigates cavity-mediated spin chains and superradiant transitions, which falls under the scope of cavity QED physics applied to magnetic/spin systems, making it highly relevant to the spintronics theme.
